en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Dukadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (6) 18.22.
Mahantaraduka, Hetuduka

Dependent on a state that has an object and is not-root, there arises a state that has no object and is not-root by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are three; under object-condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition there are three.
Dependent on a state that has an object and is not-root, there arises a state that has no object and is not-root by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that has no object and is not-root, there arises a state that has no object and is not-root by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that has an object and is not a root, and a state that has no object and is not a root, there arises a state that has no object and is not a root by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root: three; under object: three; under predominance:
one … pe … under prenascence and repetition: one … pe … under non-disappearance: three.

Dependent on a mental state that is not a cause (*no-citta*), a non-mental state that is not a cause (*na-no-citta*) arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Three [answers] for root; ... pe ... three for non-disappearance (*avigata*).
Dependent on a mental state that is not a cause, a non-mental state that is not a cause arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Three for root; ... pe ... three for non-disappearance.

Dependent on a mental factor that is a cause (*cetasika-hetu*), a non-mental-factor state that is not a cause arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Three for root; ... pe ... three for non-disappearance.

Dependent on a mental state that is neither a root-cause (*na-cetasika-nahetu*), a non-mental state that is not a root-cause arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance there are three.

Dependent on a mental state associated with consciousness that is a root-cause, a state not associated with consciousness that is not a root-cause arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are three;
under object [condition] there is one; ... pe ... under non-disappearance there are three.
Dependent on a state that is conjoined with consciousness and is a root-cause, there arises a state not conjoined with consciousness and not a root-cause, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root-condition there are three; under object-condition there is one …pe… under non-disappearance-condition there are three.
Dependent on a state that originates consciousness and is a root-cause, there arises a state not originating consciousness and not a root-cause, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-cause condition (*hetupaccaya*), there are three; ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance condition (*avigatapaccaya*), there are three. Dependent on a state that is a root cause and co-existent with consciousness (*cittasahabhu*), there arises a state that is not co-existent with consciousness and is not a root cause, by way of root-cause condition. (Abbreviated. In the case of root-cause condition, there are three; ... pe ...
in the case of non-disappearance condition, there are three.
Dependent on a state that is a root and follows the mind, there arises a state that is not a root and does not follow the mind, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Three [answers] for root; ... pe ... three for non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is a root and conjoined-with-and-produced-by-the-mind, there arises a state that is not conjoined-with-and-produced-by-the-mind and is not a root, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to the root condition (*hetu*), there are three; ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance (*avigata*), there are three.

Dependent on a state that is a root, conjoined with consciousness, generated by consciousness, and coexistent, there arises a state that is not conjoined with consciousness, not generated by consciousness, not coexistent, and not a root, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. With respect to the root condition, there are three;
... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance, there are three.

Dependent on a state that is conjoined with, originated by, and follows upon consciousness, and which is a cause, there arises a state that is not conjoined with, originated by, or following upon consciousness, and which is not a cause, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
Three for the root [condition] … pe … three for non-disappearance.

Dependent on an external state that is a cause, there arises a state that is not external and not a cause, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Three for the root [condition] … pe … three for non-disappearance.

Dependent on an internal state that is not a root-cause, there arises an external state that is neither internal nor a root-cause, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition: three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance: three.

Dependent on a state that is neither-clinging and not a root-cause, there arises a state that is neither-clinging and not a root-cause, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition: three; under object-condition: one; ... pe ... under non-disappearance: three.

Dependent on a state that is a cause of clinging (*upādāna-hetu*), a state that is not a cause of clinging and not a cause (*noupādānanahetu*) arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are three; under the object condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are three; under the predominance condition (*adhipati*) there is one ... pe ... under the prenascence and repetition conditions (*purejāta-āsevana*) there is one ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there are three.

Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and a cause (*upādinna-hetu*), a state that is neither clung-to nor a cause arises by way of the root condition ... three. Dependent on a state that is not clung-to and is a cause, a state that is neither clung-to nor a cause arises by way of the root condition.

… one. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are four; under object condition, two; under predominance condition, one … pe … under repetition condition, one … pe … under result condition, three … pe … under non-disappearance condition, four.
Dependent on a state that is clung-to and not a root, there arises a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-not-a-root by way of root condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging and is not a root-cause, there arises a state that is neither acquired by clinging nor a root-cause, by way of root-condition ...
one. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are two; under object-condition there are two; under predominance-condition there is one ... pe ... under repetition-condition there is one ...
pe ... under resultant-condition there is one ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition there are two.
